interfaces.interface_notes: The BCC phase forms at the β-Mn interfaces owing to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces; the Cu-rich FCC phase forms because of the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys and expulsion of Cu from β-Mn during its precipitation and growth. The content of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content.
interfaces.phase_evolution: The general aging sequence proposed for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels is: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase. For the 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn with a small amount of new BCC and FCC precipitates within the β-Mn.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq.
Solution-treated 17Al sample aged at 650 °C for 10 h followed by water quenching; this is the terminal state defining the sample (state label 650°C-10h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 650 °C for 10 h the α matrix of the 17Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn. The microstructure consists of an equiaxed β-Mn matrix with a small amount of new BCC and FCC Cu-rich phase precipitates distributed within the β-Mn. The volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich and BCC precipitates is 4.7 %.

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al (Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu) alloy the peak Vickers hardness of the whole series was 924.9 ± 25.8 HV, achieved at 575 °C for 6 h (Table 3), which is a different aging condition from this 650 °C/10 h sample.

The indentation fracture toughness KIC of the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h, HV = 924.9) was 6.6 MPa·m1/2, calculated using Eq. (1) with E = 175 GPa for 17Al and an average crack length of 22 μm; this value is reported for the peak-hardness (575 °C/6 h) condition, not for the 650 °C/10 h sample.

The β-Mn in the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h) contained 16.3 at.% Al, 36.2 at.% Mn and 2.6 at.% Cu, with an average intrinsic (nanoindentation) hardness of 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa and an overall nanoindentation hardness H_Ave = 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa; these values pertain to the 575 °C/6 h condition rather than the 650 °C/10 h sample.
